clue.text: Perhaps even gaiety left in consequence of the crash

indicators.note: in tells us the synonym for left goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the words even gaiety might take another form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: to have left is to have quit

explanation.surface: Even cheerfulness is a casualty of the financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges EVEN GAIETY into NEGATIVEEY, and 'in' puts QUIT inside it before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: When property prices crash, a mortgage can exceed the home's value, a state called negative equity.

clue.text: Type of art, perhaps one form to one state

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word one may appear in another arrangement

parts.note: a form is a class at school
one is the Roman numeral I
CAL is an abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: A style of art that might be described as one form belonging to one nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoclassical art is a style reviving the forms of ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Sound of bird to a king

indicators.note: to means the bird's name is attached after the royal abbreviation

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird calls out to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George (Georgius Rex), seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is a low, rumbling noise, as made by an angry dog.

clue.text: Provider of travel wherein may be nothing posh

definitions.text: Provider of travel wherein may be nothing posh

indicators.note: wherein says the following pieces sit inside the word for travel

parts.note: a trip is a journey, travel
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: may be suggests the word posh could be found in another order

explanation.surface: A ship carrying soldiers is a form of transport with nothing luxurious aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges to OPSH, and 'wherein' sets it after O inside the journey word. The whole clue also describes the answer: a no-frills ship providing travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A troopship carries soldiers, so it provides travel, and hardly in luxury.

clue.text: Richards effortlessly showing brilliance

parts.note: Viv Richards is the great West Indies cricketer
doing something idly is doing it without effort

explanation.surface: The batsman Richards plays with effortless brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Viv Richards was a famous West Indies batsman of the 1970s and 80s.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something vividly means doing it with brightness and striking intensity.

clue.text: Secure times could be clearer

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might be reshaped into another word

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A secure period could be clearer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who excuses someone clears them of blame, so an excuser is a person who clears another.

clue.text: It helps to hold one's tongue

definitions.text: It helps to hold one's tongue

parts.words: It helps to hold one's tongue
parts.note: the idiom for keeping quiet is read literally: a fleshy part at the back of the mouth hanging over the tongue

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for keeping silent is taken as a physical description of something in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvula is the small fleshy lobe hanging at the back of the soft palate above the tongue.

clue.text: Start to study a philosopher? It's a drudge

indicators.note: start picks just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to study a subject is to read it
John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: Starting to study philosophy proves to be a slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' looks like a phrase meaning begin; it takes the first letter of 'to', T.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a tiring, monotonous routine, a drudgery.

clue.text: Loves to keep book on architectural feature

indicators.note: to keep means the two loves hold the book between them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so two loves give two Os
VOL is short for volume, a book

explanation.surface: Romance novels keep a book about some feature of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a rounded convex moulding used in classical architecture.

clue.text: Swept by turns in holiday around Crete?

parts.note: VAC is short for vacation, a holiday
U-turns: each U stands for a turn
the Med, the Mediterranean, is the sea around Crete

explanation.surface: Someone is swept along by changes during a holiday around Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'in' are links. 'Turns' gives two U-turns, UU.
explanation.definitionFit: To have vacuumed a carpet is to have cleaned it, as one would have swept it.

clue.text: Labour?

parts.note: the word can mean work, or name the British political party of the workers; the question mark invites both

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a UK political party founded to represent working people.
explanation.definitionFit: A working party is a committee set up to investigate something; labour is work and the Labour Party is a party.

clue.text: Girl has room to support for pond life

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
a pad is slang for one's room or flat

explanation.surface: A young woman has space to help sustain the creatures of a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the floating leaf of a water lily, on which frogs and insects rest.

clue.text: That one may turn sad soon

indicators.note: may turn suggests the words sad soon could change into another arrangement

explanation.surface: That person may become sad shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a stand-in name for an unnamed person, that one.

clue.text: Political wannabe playing harps (Aeolian, not Old English)

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement
not means the letters for Old English are taken away from Aeolian

explanation.surface: An ambitious politician strums a harp in the Aeolian mode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes O and E from AEOLIAN, leaving ALIAN; 'playing' rearranges HARPS with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin was the 2008 US vice-presidential candidate who aspired to high office.

clue.text: Creep into organised function

indicators.note: organised means the letters of creep into are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks into a planned event.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal social function, such as after a wedding.

clue.text: Measure of Met's credit?

parts.note: the Met (London's Metropolitan Police) is based at Scotland Yard, so it is the Yard's
on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: How should the Metropolitan Police's creditworthiness be judged?
explanation.walkthrough: The Met, London's police, is known as Scotland Yard; buying on tick is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used to measure or judge something.

clue.text: How about taking an attitude to drink?

indicators.note: to means the pose-striking word is attached after the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
striking an attitude is posing

explanation.surface: Someone suggests adopting a stance towards alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposing introduces a suggestion or hypothesis, just as 'how about' or 'what if' does.

clue.text: Start to notice PIN forgery

indicators.note: a forgery is a fake reworking, so the letters of notice PIN are rearranged

explanation.surface: Begin by spotting a fake bank-card number.
explanation.definitionFit: Inception means the beginning or start of something.

clue.text: Near the coast we're told to get cover

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to insure is to get insurance cover

explanation.surface: Being close to the shore, we are advised to take out insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for getting cover is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore means close to or towards the shore.

clue.text: With most elderly, fun may be requisite

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form another word
most means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: elderly people are older, elder

explanation.surface: For most of the old, having fun may be essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims ELDER to ELDE; 'may be' rearranges ELDE with FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means necessary or required, like requisite.

clue.text: See 13
Aims at less than what Cockney does without

indicators.note: less than means a word taken away from the longer one

parts.note: a Cockney drops his H sounds, the aspirates

explanation.surface: Someone aims for less than a Cockney manages without.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speakers of East London famously drop their aitches; an aitch is an aspirate.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire to something is to aim at it ambitiously.

clue.text: Rule: to abdicate lacks point

indicators.note: lacks means the compass point goes missing from the longer word

parts.note: to abdicate is to resign a throne
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The law of abdication has no point.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's period of rule.

clue.text: English lose balance after attempt to boost self-esteem

indicators.note: after places the word for losing balance behind the word for attempt

parts.note: a go is an attempt
to trip is to lose one's balance

explanation.surface: An Englishman stumbles after trying to feel better about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done mainly to make oneself feel important.

clue.text: It's partly intended to cure habits

definitions.text: It's partly intended to cure habits

indicators.note: partly signals that only part of the words cure habits is used

explanation.surface: Treatment aimed in part at breaking addictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'cuRE HABits', and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is treatment to overcome addictions.

clue.text: Informal greeting by smart type without it having to get friendly

parts.note: hi is a casual hello

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the toff surrounds the word it

parts.note: a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class person

explanation.surface: A casual hello from a posh person without it leads to friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit it off is an idiom meaning to get on well at once.

clue.text: Sometimes I chortle at watery humour

indicators.note: sometimes says only some of the letters of I chortle are used

explanation.surface: I occasionally laugh at weak comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' looks like comedy but is a bodily fluid, as in medieval medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is a thin watery discharge from a wound, a fluid or humour of the body.

clue.text: Loveless union on the box contains one big long mistake in a way defying interpretation

indicators.note: Loveless asks for love, zero in tennis and so the letter O, to be removed from the next word
contains means the television word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: the box is slang for television, the telly
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: mistake means the letters are wrongly placed, rearranged

explanation.surface: A loveless marriage watched on television contains one huge error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' gives UNIN. 'mistake' rearranges the pieces into GIBL, and 'contains' sets them, after I, between TELL and Y. The box is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Done unintelligibly means done in a way no one can understand or interpret.
